title: Descent of point-indexed equalizer charts and finite étale stalks
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $X$ a $k$-scheme with a finite affine open cover $U_j=\operatorname{Spec}B_j$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $h:X\to X$ a $k$-endomorphism preserving each $U_j$. Let $\phi_j:B_j\to B_j$ be the induced $k$-algebra map and $J_j=(\phi_j(b)-b:b\in B_j)$. Let $P$ be a set with a family of $k$-points $x_p:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ satisfying $h\circ x_p=x_p$. Put $P_j=\{p\in P:x_p\text{ factors through }U_j\}$. Assume that each $P_j$ is finite and that the evaluations at these points induce an isomorphism of $k$-algebras $B_j/J_j\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{p\in P_j}k$. Let $F$ be the equalizer of $h$ and $1_X$, defined by $X\times_{X\times_kX,(1,h),\Delta_X}X$ with its first projection $i:F\to X$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $P$ is finite and the unique map $\coprod_{p\in P}\operatorname{Spec}k\to F$ whose composite with $i$ on the $p$-th summand is $x_p$ is an isomorphism. Its restriction over $U_j$ is the spectrum of the prescribed evaluation isomorphism, using the canonical spectrum-of-finite-product identification. This description is compatible on all open overlaps, without assuming that the overlaps are affine or that $X$ is separated. The structure morphism of $F$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and étale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. For every point $z\in F$, the structural map $k\to\mathcal O_{F,z}$ is an isomorphism and $\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{F,z}}\mathcal O_{F,z}=1$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Empty $X$ and $P$ are allowed. Here an ideal of a ring $R$ is an additive subgroup stable under multiplication by elements of $R$; $(S)$ denotes the ideal of finite sums of ring multiples of elements of $S$, and $R/L$ is the quotient by $u\sim v\iff u-v\in L$.

proof.text: Every $p\in P$ belongs to some $P_j$, since the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ maps into some member of the given cover; its map factors through that open by the definition of an open subscheme. Thus $P=\bigcup_jP_j$ is a finite union of finite sets. The fibre-product universal property defining $F$ says that maps $T\to F$ are precisely maps $a:T\to X$ with $ha=a$: the second projection must equal $a$, and the other equation is $ha=a$. In particular $i$ is a monomorphism. Each $x_p$ therefore lifts uniquely to $y_p:\operatorname{Spec}k\to F$. By the coproduct mapping property these lifts define a unique map $q:D=\coprod_{p\in P}\operatorname{Spec}k\to F$ with $iq$ equal to the prescribed point map on every summand.

source.place: Step 0: equalizer as fibre product; Step 2: canonical point-indexed maps

proof.text: Put $E_j=F\times_XU_j$ and write $\pi_j:\operatorname{Spec}(B_j/I_j)\to U_j$ for the quotient map. The graph equations imply that $i:F\to X$ is monic and equalizes $h$ and the identity. The quotient map equalizes the induced endomorphism, since each difference lies in $I_j$, so it lifts first to $F$ and then to $E_j$. Conversely, for any test scheme $T$ and map $a:T\to U_j$ equalizing the endomorphism, naturality of the spectrum-global-sections adjunction implies that the map $B_j\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ kills every difference, and hence $I_j$. Mathlib's Scheme.Hom.liftQuotient gives its factorization through $\pi_j$ directly, without an affine cover of $T$. Apply this to the second projection of $E_j$ to construct the inverse. The two inverse equations follow by cancellation: $\pi_j$ is a closed immersion and the second projection of $E_j$ is a base change of the monomorphism $i$. This constructs $e_j:\operatorname{Spec}(B_j/I_j)\simeq E_j$ with the required second projection.

source.place: Step 0: affine difference-ideal description and compatibility with open restriction; expanded universal-property argument

proof.text: The finite-product spectrum isomorphism sigmaSpec, followed by $\operatorname{Spec}(\varepsilon_j)$ and $e_j$, gives an isomorphism $v_j:D_j=\coprod_{p\in P_j}\operatorname{Spec}k\simeq E_j$. Its composite on the $p$-th summand with $E_j\to F\to X$ is $x_p$, by the evaluation normalization $h\varepsilon$. Since $i:F\to X$ is monic, this composite to $F$ is precisely the canonical lift $y_p$. Each $y_p$ is an open immersion: choose a chart containing $p$ and express it as a coprojection followed by $v_j$ and the open immersion $E_j\to F$. These maps jointly cover $F$: choose a chart at the image of a point of $F$, lift the point to $E_j$ using the range formula for a pullback of an open immersion, and then use the isomorphism $v_j$ and the coproduct open cover. The same equality on coprojections gives exactly the required displayed chart-restriction equation for $q$.

source.place: Step 2: evaluation projections give the canonical point maps and factors belonging to an open

proof.text: The open images of the $y_p$ are pairwise disjoint. Indeed, if $y_p(a)=y_r(b)=z$, choose a chart $U_j$ at $i(z)$. Since $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has one point, both $x_p$ and $x_r$ factor through this chart by the universal property of an open immersion, so $p,r\in P_j$. The chart equation identifies $y_p(a)$ and $y_r(b)$ with the images of the two coprojections under the injective map $D_j\simeq E_j\to F$. Disjointness of the coproduct summands forces $p=r$. Mathlib's isOpenImmersion_sigmaDesc now makes $q=\operatorname{Sigma.desc}(y_p)$ an open immersion, and the preceding covering assertion makes it surjective. A surjective open immersion is an isomorphism. Finally, for arbitrary test schemes and any two chart maps whose composites to $X$ agree, cancellation of the monomorphism $i$ proves their composites to $F$ agree. This is the stated overlap compatibility and needs neither affine overlaps nor separatedness.

source.place: Steps 0 and 2: Zariski descent, with the explicit inverse-gluing argument

proof.text: Coproduct extensionality and $x_p\circ s=1$ identify $q\mathbin{\gg}(i\mathbin{\gg}s)$ with sigmaSpec followed by the spectrum of the diagonal algebra map $k\to\prod_{p\in P}k$. This is a finite ring map, since the finite product of one-dimensional $k$-modules is finite as a module. Mathlib's IsFinite.SpecMap_iff and stability under composition show that the displayed composite is finite. Composing with $q^{-1}$ proves the assertion for $i\mathbin{\gg}s$. The finite-product argument includes the empty index set and its zero ring.

source.place: Step 3: finiteness of the finite disjoint union, written using its product algebra

proof.text: The identity extension $k/k$ is finite separable (dimension one, with linear minimal polynomials). Apply the coproduct-of-finite-separable-field-spectra lemma with $L_p=k$ to conclude that $D\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is étale, also for the empty index set. Since $q$ is a $k$-isomorphism, this is exactly the étaleness assertion for $F$.

source.place: Tag 02GL, label lemma-etale-over-field, converse direction, specialized to identity extensions; blueprint Step 3

proof.text: Each point of $F$ has the form $y_p(a)$ for one of the open immersions $y_p:\operatorname{Spec}k\to F$. The stalk map of this open immersion is an isomorphism. Naturality of germs and $y_p\mathbin{\gg}i\mathbin{\gg}s=1$ identify its composite with the structural map $k\to\mathcal O_{F,y_p(a)}$ with the canonical map from $k$ to the stalk of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ at $a$. This last map is an isomorphism: the stalk is localization at a prime of $k$, and Field.localization_map_bijective says localization of a field away from zero is bijective. Cancel the isomorphism on stalks to obtain exactly the structural stalk-map isomorphism in the conclusion. Its induced ring equivalence transports the field property to the stalk; a field is simple as a module over itself, so Module.length_eq_one gives length one. The proof uses no nonempty assumption on $F$, and is vacuous when $F$ is empty.
